topics.title: Welcome to Magic Git
topics.summary: Overview of Magic Git's native macOS interface, workspace multi-tab concept, and core capabilities.

sections.text: Magic Git is a native macOS Git desktop client designed for extreme performance, safety, and modern software engineering workflows. It provides a tabbed multi-repository workspace, SSH connection manager, interactive commit graph, and built-in Forge integrations.
Native macOS Architecture

Magic Git combines Flutter for high-refresh-rate UI rendering with native Swift AppKit/SwiftUI controllers for system menu integration, security-scoped sandbox bookmarks, multi-window isolation, and native support documentation.

sections.title: App Sandbox Security
sections.text: Local repository access in Magic Git uses macOS security-scoped bookmarks, ensuring full compliance with Apple Sandbox privacy rules.

topics.title: Connecting to Repositories
topics.summary: Learn how to open local Git repositories and connect to remote hosts over SSH.

sections.text: Local Repositories

To open a local repository, click Open Local Folder on the landing screen or use the Connections panel. Magic Git requests folder access via a standard macOS open panel and saves a security-scoped bookmark for subsequent app launches.
Remote SSH Repositories
Magic Git supports direct remote SSH operations. Enter your SSH host, username, port, and key path. Private keys with passphrases and host key verification prompts are fully supported.

sections.title: Automatic Reconnection
sections.text: If a remote SSH connection drops mid-session, Magic Git displays a background retry banner with a live reconnect timer without losing your local work state.

topics.title: Repository (Status & Staging) Tab
topics.summary: Stage changes, view line diffs, discard modifications, and commit HEAD updates.

sections.text: The Repository tab (⌘1) displays working tree modifications organized into Staged Changes and Unstaged Changes lists.
Staging & Discarding

items: Press Space on any file row to toggle staging for that file.
Use ⌘⇧A to stage all tracked and untracked modifications.
Use ⌘⇧⌫ to discard unstaged changes on the selected file after confirmation.
Drag to select specific diff lines in the right pane for partial hunk staging.

sections.text: Diff Inspection & Committing
Toggle between inline diff view and side-by-side split view using ⌥⌘S. Enter your commit subject and description in the bottom pane. Toggle 'Amend last commit' or press ⌘↩ to rewrite HEAD.

sections.title: Co-Authors
sections.text: You can add Git Co-authored-by trailers directly from the commit editor prior to committing.

topics.title: History & Commit Graph Tab
topics.summary: Explore commit history, topological graph lanes, filter commits, and perform branch mutations.

sections.text: The History tab (⌘2) renders an interactive topological commit graph with colored branch lanes, ref tags, and commit metadata.
All Branches Scope vs HEAD Scope

Click the All Branches button in the History toolbar to toggle between git log --all and git log HEAD. When All Branches is active, merged and cut feature branches across the repository history are rendered. This toggle has no keyboard shortcut — ⌘⇧B is Checkout Selected Commit, which asks for confirmation before checking out.
Commit Actions & Secondary Windows

items: Right-click or select a commit to open actions: Checkout, Create Branch, Create Tag, Cherry-pick, and Revert.
Click 'Open History in New Window' or press ⌘⇧H to pop out a dedicated, floating history window that updates live.

sections.title: Live Updates
sections.text: The History view listens to repository file system events and automatically refreshes when refs or branch tips move.

topics.title: Branches & Merging Tab
topics.summary: Manage local and remote tracking branches, create new branches, merge, rebase, and sync remotes.

sections.text: The Branches tab (⌘3) provides full control over local branches, remote tracking branches, and branch integration.
Branch Operations

items: Press ⌘B to create a new branch from current HEAD.
Double-click a branch to check it out.
Select a branch and press ⌘⇧M to merge it into your active branch.
Use the context menu to Rebase active branch onto target branch or Delete (⌘⌫).

sections.title: Unmerged Branch Deletion
sections.text: Deleting an unmerged branch prompts for confirmation to prevent accidental loss of unmerged commit history.

topics.title: Stashes Tab
topics.summary: Save uncommitted modifications to the stash stack, inspect diff previews, apply, pop, and drop stashes.

sections.text: The Stashes tab (⌘4) allows temporary shelving of working tree modifications without creating formal commits.
Creating & Inspecting Stashes
Click 'Stash Changes' to specify a custom message and optionally include untracked files. Select any stash in the list to view its commit hash, branch context, and modified file diffs.
Applying & Popping

items: Apply (⌥⌘A): Restores stashed changes to your working directory while leaving the stash in the stack.
Pop: Restores stashed changes and removes the stash entry from the stack.
Drop: Permanently deletes the selected stash entry.

topics.title: Forge (GitHub & GitLab) Tab
topics.summary: Inspect Pull Requests, Merge Requests, CI/CD pipeline runs, issues, and live build trace logs.

sections.text: The Forge tab (⌘5) integrates directly with GitHub (`gh` CLI/API) and GitLab (`glab` CLI/API) hosts.
Pull / Merge Request Workflows

items: Filter PRs/MRs by status (Open, Merged, Closed, Mine).
View full title, description, author, review approvals, and changed file diffs.
Click 'Checkout Branch' to locally check out a PR/MR's head branch with one click.

sections.text: CI/CD Pipeline Monitoring
Inspect live GitHub Actions workflows or GitLab CI pipeline runs. Click any job to stream ANSI-formatted execution trace logs in real time.

topics.title: Worktrees Tab
topics.summary: Create and manage multiple concurrent Git worktrees for parallel branch development.

sections.text: The Worktrees tab (⌘6) enables working on multiple branches simultaneously in separate filesystem folders.
Adding Worktrees
Click 'Add Worktree' to check out a branch into a target directory. Magic Git automatically creates a security-scoped bookmark for the new worktree path.

sections.title: Tab Integration
sections.text: Opening a worktree loads it as a tab in your multi-tab workspace, allowing seamless switching without changing branch state in your main directory.

topics.title: Remote SSH & Host Verification
topics.summary: Secure remote Git operations over SSH with key passphrases and host key verification.

sections.text: Magic Git includes a custom SSH command executor and transport manager supporting public-key authentication, encrypted private keys, and custom SSH ports.
Host Key Verification Prompts
When connecting to a new remote host or if a server's fingerprint changes, Magic Git displays an SSH Host Key prompt showing the trusted vs presented fingerprints before establishing a connection.

topics.title: Command Palette & Keymap
topics.summary: Search all actions, run panel commands, and customize global keyboard shortcuts.

sections.text: Press ⌘K or ⌘P anywhere in the application to summon the Command Palette. Type to search commands, branch names, worktrees, or settings.
Global Undo Engine
Magic Git maintains a global undo stack. Destructive actions (such as staging, discarding, branch switches, or stash drops) present an Undo Toast notification (`⌘Z` to reverse).

topics.title: Tool Health & Environment
topics.summary: Check system availability and binary paths for git, ssh, gh, and glab.

sections.text: Magic Git checks for system dependencies on startup. If a required binary is missing from PATH, a Tool Health Banner appears at the top of the window with installation guidance.

topics.title: Output Log & Command Recovery
topics.summary: View real-time command execution output, stdout/stderr streams, and exit codes.

sections.text: Open the Output Log (⌘⇧O) or Recovery View (⌘⇧U) from the View menu to inspect raw Git/SSH command invocations, stdout output, stderr traces, and exit statuses.
